reason: This book (long XLF, long XBI, short SOXL, short GDX, 15% cash) is a domestic sector relative-value bet against two mean-reversion candidates -- leveraged semis and gold miners -- and the single biggest piece of new information gathered today (research into the 2026-09-16 FOMC) reinforces rather than undermines that bet, so trading into it would just be churn. Market pricing has swung sharply hawkish: the Investing.com Fed Rate Monitor shows ~90% odds of a hike to 3.75-4.00% rather than a cut, and news coverage attributes the shift to new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole tone plus a stronger-than-expected August jobs report -- a possible first hike since 2023. That is directly supportive of both short legs: higher/higher-for-longer real rates are a classic headwind for non-yielding gold, and GDX-specific reporting today explicitly notes 'the bull rally in precious metals has run out of steam,' which is exactly the overextension thesis this leg was built on (it is already +4.25% since 09-08 with a -15%/+20% bracket doing its job). SOXL, a 3x leveraged long-semis ETF, is high-beta to exactly the kind of valuation-multiple compression a hawkish rate shock produces, and that leg is already the book's best performer this cycle (+14.64%) with its own -15%/+20% bracket intact. The two long legs are more mixed but not broken: XLF (financials) is close to flat (-0.66%) and higher rates are typically constructive for bank net-interest margins even if a hawkish surprise causes a broad risk-off wobble first; XBI (biotech) is the one leg genuinely at risk from a hawkish shock since higher discount rates compress long-duration biotech valuations, and it is down -3.82% this leg, but it still has 6+ points of room to its -10% stop and a real, dated catalyst (the FOMC decision itself, landing 2026-09-16) is exactly the kind of event where letting a pre-set stop do the job beats a discretionary pre-emptive cut based on the same information the stop was already sized for. All four legs already carry both a stop and a take-profit, so the book's risk is fully bounded going into the decision without me touching anything, and a full or partial replacement here would spend real basis points (2bps/side equities, plus the book is unlevered so no leverage-related urgency) to express a view the current stops and weights already express. Holding lets the FOMC outcome resolve through the existing bracket orders rather than through a discretionary re-guess of the same macro call the book was built on.
